html:
SMTO-SKL-0112 — This Slack sign-in link is no longer valid

GUID: edb6ef33-c090-57ff-b9fe-01894886827d
Slug: slack-oauth-state-invalid
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • Slack sent you back to SMTO, but SMTO had no open sign-in waiting for that reply. The link may be old, already used, or cleared when SMTO restarted. No Slack workspace was connected by this attempt.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Close any old Slack sign-in tabs, and don't reuse sign-in links from earlier messages or bookmarks. Each link works only once, and only for the sign-in request that created it.
  2. Ask SMTO to connect Slack again, then open the new link and finish Slack's page within 10 minutes. A fresh link creates a new sign-in that SMTO is actually waiting for.
  3. Don't restart SMTO or edit the Slack OAuth App entry in Parameter Store until the page says you're connected. SMTO forgets unfinished sign-ins when it restarts and rejects them if the app entry changes meanwhile.
  4. If it keeps failing, tell the person who manages SMTO which web address you use to open SMTO. Slack must send you back to exactly the address saved in the app entry, or SMTO can't match the reply.

What success looks like

  • The Slack sign-in tab shows a message starting with "Connected" that says you can close the window.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep reloading the old sign-in page, and don't paste sign-in links or codes from the address bar into a conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Slack browser authorization rejected the callback or launch ticket: unknown, malformed or already used state (including state lost on Server restart), duplicate code/state/error parameters, a callback URL different from the pending redirect_uri, or a Slack OAuth App record changed during the flow.

What this means

  • Callback parameters are duplicated, or shared OAuth state is malformed, missing, consumed or bound to a different redirect URI. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Callback parameters are duplicated, or shared OAuth state is malformed, missing, consumed or bound to a different redirect URI.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect callback parameter names, exact redirect and pending-state lifecycle without logging state/code values.

How to fix it

  • Start a new slack.connect and complete it once: pending state is single-use, held only in Server memory for 600 seconds, and lost on restart. If it recurs, confirm the externally seen callback URL (scheme, host and port behind any proxy) exactly equals the profile's redirect_uri, that nothing duplicates the code, state or error query parameters, and that the slack_oauth_app record is not edited between start and callback.
  • Restart slack.connect and finish the newly issued browser flow on the exact configured callback URL; old state is single-use.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A new single-use consent flow completes on its exact registered callback.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
